scope: Proposition 4.10 (All-point boundary-chain estimate) of the manuscript “The critical Liouville quantum sphere and geometric limits of FK maps at q=4” (preprints/The-critical-Liouville-quantum-sphere-and-geometric-limits-of-FK-maps-at-q-equals-4-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b9236021eab20eb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a disk g in standard twice-typical strip coordinates with perimeter s, paths in its interior approaching any flat boundary point z and +∞ can be joined, along the direction to the right, at cost bounded (including the above deterministic upper weight) by K s2ξ0/γ (︃ m([z, +∞)) s )︃θ2ξ0/γ , (4.1) where m denotes boundary length on that side. The moment quantifier is as follows: for each M ∈ (0, ∞), choose θ < 1 sufficiently close to 1 and then γM < 2 so that sup γ∈(γM ,2] E[KM ] < ∞. The value γ = 2 denotes the limiting disk law. The choice of θ is allowed to depend on M. More precisely we assert existence of connected chains/paths between arbitrarily small neighborhoods of the two points, simultaneously at every z. The reverse statement toward −∞ also holds, and the chains may approach an end on either side using central Whitney slab paths. No exact internal metric extension to boundary is needed.
